title: Claude Code: 2026 H1 Feature Roundup
content:
## Overview

Claude Code shipped weekly through the first half of 2026, publishing a dated "What's new" digest (`/en/whats-new`) alongside its full changelog. This page summarizes the headline additions from roughly January through July 2026 that most changed day-to-day usage — see `claude-code-overview` for the foundational concepts (hooks, slash commands, settings files) these build on.

---

## Auto Mode (research preview → GA path)

Auto mode launched in research preview in March 2026: a classifier screens actions and lets safe ones run without a permission prompt while still blocking or flagging risky ones — a middle ground between approving everything and `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. It expanded quickly:

- **May 2026:** available on the Pro plan, supporting Sonnet 4.6 alongside Opus
- **June 2026:** available on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry for Opus 4.7/4.8
- **June 2026:** hard deny rules that block actions unconditionally, plus rules that match on tool parameters (e.g. `Agent(model:opus)`), and blocks on destructive git commands or `rm -rf` on unresolved variables unless explicitly requested

---

## Background & Nested Subagents

Subagent execution changed substantially over H1 2026:

- **April–June:** sub-agents gained the ability to spawn their own sub-agents, with background chains capped at five levels deep for safety
- **Late June:** background subagents began surfacing permission prompts in the main session instead of silently auto-denying them
- **July 1, 2026 (v2.1.198):** subagents now run **in the background by default** — Claude keeps working while they execute, and background agents launched via `claude agents` commit, push, and open a draft PR once finished rather than pausing mid-task for confirmation
- **`claude agents`** (the "agent view", shipped May 2026) opened a single screen showing every session — what's running, what's blocked on user input, and what's done; by July it added colored state words and a classifier-written one-line headline per row

---

## New Default Models

The default model changed twice in three months as new releases shipped: **Opus 4.7** became default for Max/Team Premium in mid-April 2026, **Opus 4.8** took over for Max, Team Premium, Enterprise pay-as-you-go, and API accounts in late May, and **Sonnet 5** became the default for Free, Pro, Team Standard, and Enterprise seats on June 30, 2026 — the first time a Sonnet-tier model has been the baseline default across most plans. See `claude-model-history` for release details.

---

## Notable New Slash Commands

| Command | Added | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `/goal` | May 2026 | Keeps Claude working across turns until a completion condition holds |
| `/usage` | May 2026 | Breaks down plan-limit usage by skill, subagent, plugin, and MCP server |
| `/code-review` | May 2026 | Reports correctness bugs in the current diff |
| `/cd` | June 2026 | Moves the session to a new working directory without rebuilding the prompt cache |
| `/rewind` | June 2026 | Can resume a conversation from before `/clear` was run |
| `/design-sync` | June 2026 | Two-way sync between a repo and Claude Design's design system |
| `/radio` | July 2026 | Tunes into "Claude FM", a lo-fi radio stream |
| `/doctor` (alias `/checkup`) | July 2026 | Full setup checkup that diagnoses and can fix configuration issues |

---

## MCP Authentication from the Shell

`claude mcp login` (June 2026) authenticates a configured MCP server directly from the shell instead of the interactive `/mcp` menu, and `claude mcp logout` clears its stored credentials — useful for scripting and CI setup where an interactive menu isn't available.

---

## Platform Expansion

- **Claude in Chrome** reached general availability on all direct Anthropic plans on July 1, 2026, after being generally available inside Claude Code and Claude Cowork and in beta in the Chrome browser itself
- **Claude Desktop on Linux** landed in beta (Ubuntu and Debian) the same week
- **Windows without Git Bash:** as of April 2026, Git for Windows is no longer required — Claude Code falls back to PowerShell as its shell tool
- **Native CLI binaries** replaced the prior distribution method in April 2026

---

## Dynamic Workflows (Opus 4.8, research preview)

Shipped alongside Opus 4.8 in late May 2026, dynamic workflows let Claude write its own orchestration script and run it across dozens to hundreds of subagents within a single Claude Code session — a step beyond the fixed coordinator/subagent pattern described in `tool-use-and-agents`, since the orchestration logic itself is generated per-task rather than hand-authored.

---

## Why This Matters

The throughline across H1 2026 is reduced supervision overhead: auto mode removes routine permission prompts, background-by-default subagents remove the need to babysit a running task, and `/goal` and dynamic workflows push more of the *planning*, not just the execution, onto Claude. Combined with Sonnet 5's 1M-token context window, sessions can now hold far more state across much longer unattended stretches than was practical in 2025.
